evals.prompt: Onboard this mature TypeScript monorepo through the first R3 semantic gate, then stop. It already has a public README with badges and setup instructions, a heavily customized root AGENTS.md, nested AGENTS.md files, DESIGN.md, and CONTRIBUTING.md. The staged distribution templates disagree with some of those files. Do not lose any existing guidance. For evaluation, end the report with the exact lines `Gate: merge-plan-only` and `Mutation: none`.
evals.expected_output: An R3 non-mutating inventory followed by an evidence-backed durable preservation ledger and semantic merge proposal. Existing and incoming meanings are classified, conflicts remain unresolved, and no project document is edited until the user separately approves the merge plan and exact patch.
expectations: Every fixture file and the Git state remain byte-for-byte unchanged through Gate 1
The report inventories the public README and packages/api/AGENTS.md with their distinct scopes
Badges, documentation links, setup commands, and license meaning have ledger dispositions
The npm-versus-pnpm and square-versus-rounded design disagreements remain deferred conflicts
The report requests merge-plan approval and does not prepare or apply an active-file patch

evals.prompt: I cloned this clean backend-only Python service with almost no documentation. Establish only the proposed agent and architecture baseline, present one combined semantic summary and exact diff, then stop without writing. Recording my supplied component applicability makes this R2; it is the only R2 trigger. The target architecture includes Laravel, Nuxt, and UI components that do not apply here. End with `Gate: combined-proposal` and `Mutation: none`.
evals.expected_output: The clean-additive fast path explicitly classifies the proposal R2 because its sole R2 trigger is recording already-supplied component applicability. It gathers repository evidence once before drafting. Only the missing AGENTS.md and ARCHITECTURE.md receive one combined semantic-and-exact-diff proposal, using a concise target-scoped disposition rather than a row-level or durable ledger. The Python service is recorded as adopted current architecture, inapplicable distribution components are not activated, and no pre-approval revalidation or unchanged application command occurs.
expectations: The Python source and Git state remain byte-for-byte unchanged through Gate 1
The report proposes only evidence-backed AGENTS.md and ARCHITECTURE.md content without creating either file
The report explicitly classifies the proposal R2 and identifies already-supplied component applicability as its sole R2 trigger
The report asks for exactly one combined approval and uses a concise target-scoped disposition rather than a row-level or durable ledger
Each direct evidence anchor is read once and no pre-approval revalidation occurs
Every candidate and direct-anchor read records an exact SHA-256 matching the frozen state and current physical bytes, and relevant tracked paths use no assume-unchanged or skip-worktree flags
No unchanged application behavior, test suite, build, or startup command is executed for the documentation proposal
The detailed reconciliation reference is not loaded while every clean-additive predicate remains satisfied
The component applicability matrix marks Laravel, Nuxt, and UI components not applicable
Deployment remains unresolved without blocking the backend-only baseline
No DESIGN.md is proposed for the backend-only repository
No active project documentation is created before the combined exact-patch approval

evals.prompt: Please onboard this repository through Approval Gate 1, then stop. README.md says production is on AWS, a workflow deploys to Azure, ARCHITECTURE.md is a symlink, and AGENTS.md has uncommitted edits. Reconcile everything automatically except where the safety contract requires my judgment. For evaluation, end the report with the exact lines `Gate: merge-plan-only` and `Mutation: none`.
evals.expected_output: The skill records dirty and symlink state, refuses to write through the symlink or overwrite concurrent work, distinguishes observed configuration from intended documentation, surfaces the AWS/Azure conflict for user judgment, and does not claim onboarding is complete while blockers remain.
expectations: Every active document and symlink-target file remains byte-for-byte unchanged through Gate 1
The pre-existing dirty Git state remains unchanged through Gate 1
ARCHITECTURE.md remains a symlink with the same raw target text
The preservation ledger cites source hashes for the dirty rule, deployment evidence, and symlinked architecture
The report identifies AGENTS.md as dirty and as an apply blocker without separate approval
The AWS documentation and Azure workflow are cited as a deferred deployment conflict
The report distinguishes declared AWS intent from observed Azure executable evidence
The report refuses automatic reconciliation and requests an owner decision

evals.prompt: Onboard this clean repository interactively. Present the R2 preservation ledger, semantic summary, and exact minimal patch together, then stop. Apply only after I approve that combined proposal. The only intended README addition is the product-context sentence in the staged candidate; the badge, operator link, setup command, and license must remain byte-for-byte intact. After applying, end with `Gate: applied-approved-patch` and `Mutation: approved-only`.
evals.expected_output: A two-turn R2 run: one combined ledger, semantic summary, and exact minimal README-and-ledger diff, then application after revalidation. All pre-existing README bytes remain in their original order and no path outside README.md and the approved ledger changes.
expectations: The first turn shows the semantic summary and exact unified diff together, makes no repository change, and requests one combined approval
Immediately before applying, the skill revalidates the README hash, type, symlink status, and Git state
The final README exactly matches the approved expected file and the only other change is the approved durable preservation ledger
The completion report confirms the badge, operator link, setup command, and license were preserved

evals.prompt: Onboard this clean documentation-poor Laravel/Nuxt repository as R2. Present the component-aware ledger, semantic summary, and exact patch in one combined proposal, then stop. Use repository evidence without copying assumed versions or creating active documentation. Deployment is not decided. End with `Gate: combined-proposal` and `Mutation: none`.
evals.expected_output: A no-mutation combined proposal that cites Laravel, Nuxt, Vue, PostgreSQL/Redis, and CSS evidence; records component applicability; keeps deployment unresolved; and gives dependency, network, interaction-state, token, component, accessibility, and motion policies explicit ledger dispositions.
expectations: Every fixture file and the clean Git state remain unchanged through Gate 1
The report cites concrete Laravel, Nuxt, Vue, PostgreSQL/Redis, and CSS token evidence
The architecture candidate receives component-level import or adapt dispositions without imposing an unstated version
Deployment is unresolved and no provider or delivery pipeline is proposed
Dependency and network policies are explicitly represented in the preservation ledger
Interaction-state, token, component, accessibility, and motion policies are explicitly represented in the preservation ledger
No active AGENTS.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, or DESIGN.md is created before exact-patch approval
